Kareedouw Kliphuis Mystery

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... two unexplained deaths

Unique Selling Point:
Mystery deaths --in a holiday home

Summary:
he South African Police in Kareedouw have opened an inquest following the death of a couple on a farm in the Kareedouw area.
According to police information, the couple and a friend were on the farm Zuuranys, for the weekend. They were staying in a house that is rented out for weekends – a holiday house. It is alleged that the couple went to shower late on Saturday, 25 April 2020 and the friend went to bed. When the friend woke up on Sunday, 26 April 2020, at about 09:00, he noticed that the couple was not in their room. The friend went to the bathroom and discovered that the door was locked from the inside.
He kicked in the door and discovered the bodies of the 26-year-old man and his 28-year-old female friend.

Further information:
FIRST REPORTS
The South African Police in Kareedouw have opened an inquest following the death of a couple on a farm in the Kareedouw area.
According to police information, the couple and a friend were on the farm Zuuranys, for the weekend. They were staying in a house that is rented out for weekends – a holiday house.
It is alleged that the couple went to shower late on Saturday, 25 April 2020 and the friend went to bed.
When the friend woke up on Sunday, 26 April 2020, at about 09:00, he noticed that the couple was not in their room. The friend went to the bathroom and discovered that the door was locked from the inside.
He kicked in the door and discovered the bodies of the 26-year-old man and his 28-year-old female friend.
The police were immediately summoned to the scene and an inquest was opened.
No foul play is suspected and the exact cause of death will be determined by the post mortem.
++++++++
The couple who died tragically was Jean Vosloo and Mari Hoon and they were engaged.
When the news broke, three more groups of people who stayed over in the Kliphuis and experienced strange effects, in fact they nearly died there. In two instances people lost consciousness in the bathroom while showering and were saved in the nick of time. In another case a man woke up in the night with a massive headache and found his wife unconscious next to him. He was able to revive her once they got outside.
The post- mortem yielded no results – the coroner could not find anything. However, blood samples were taken and sent off for analysis. Results are expected in a couple of years.
In the meantime, families sit with unanswered questions, and the mystery deaths could be repeated if more people were to stay in that particular holiday house.
But with no toxicology reports, the inquest cannot continue and investigations have ground to a halt.
Dr Lawton Vosloo, father of Jean, has asked a gas expert to examine the scene, and is disappointed that the coroner would not allow him access to blood samples so it could be tested independently.

Press Release:


The Kliphuis Mystery
A holiday house in the Eastern Cape has become the site of an intractable mystery after a young couple was found dead in its bathroom. Without any obvious cause of death or injuries, even the post-mortems couldn’t give families closure. With delays at forensic laboratories, answers can take years – but after the incident hit the media, several more people came forward, reporting blackouts in the same room. Carte Blanche investigates whether carbon-monoxide poisoning could be the cause of such grief.
Producer: Eugene Botha
Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


V/O:
This is the last photograph of Jean Vosloo and his fiancé Mari Hoon. It was taken at a holiday cottage on a farm in the Eastern Cape on the 25th of April…a few short hours later, they would both be dead.

Jean and Mari were staying overnight, with a friend Steefan du Toit, in the Kouga Kliphuis on the banks of the Kouga River.
LINK:
Early on the morning of the 26th the friend started looking for them. They were not in their bedroom. He called out for them, but they did not answer. Then he found that the bathroom was locked from the inside.
V/O:
Du Toit kicked the door in and found them lifeless in the shower. He rushed to call the Kareedouw Police. Jean and Mari were certified dead on the scene. There was no apparent cause of death.

Du Toit was traumatised by the incident and declined to speak to us about it.

Jean’s parents, Dr Lawton Vosloo and his wife Christel were enjoying Sunday brunch when Christel’s phone rang. It was a police officer from Kareedouw.
Christel Vosloo:
En hy sê: “Ek wil jou net laat weet jou seun is oorlede”. En ek kon dit nie glo nie. Ek het net gesê, “Nee, Nee,Nee! Dit kan nie wees nie. My kind kan nie dood wees nie”.
V/O:
The officer informed them that Mari was also dead. Jean and Mari had met at University. They were young and fit…and planning a future together. Their sudden demise was a complete mystery.
Lawton Vosloo:
So young people do not die of natural causes in a shower.
V/O:
Vosloo suspected that something at the Kliphuis caused their deaths and hoped that the post-mortems would provide the answer. He went to speak to the physician who performed the autopsies.
Lawton Vosloo:
She said they suspect no foul play; they can’t find the cause of death.
V/O:
Blood samples were taken and were sent away for toxicological analysis in the hope it would reveal the cause of death.

But toxicology results from the National Health Laboratory Service can take years, because of huge backlogs, says Dr Reggie Perumal, a private Forensic Pathologist.
Dr. Reggie Perumal:
In South Africa, all I can say it takes a very long time to get a result. At some stage it took 6 years to get a report.
V/O:
Dr. Vosloo suspected that carbon monoxide poisoning could be the cause of death – but only a toxicology report could confirm it.

When the story broke in the media, Vosloo’s phone soon rang again – this time it was people reporting strange experiences at the Kliphuis.
Lawton Vosloo:
Friends of friends of friends said to me they were in the same place, in the same house. They were is the exact same Klliphuis and they had narrow escapes.
V/O
Taryn Janks and Jonathan Hill stayed in the Kliphuis for a weekend in August last year. While showering, Taryn suffered a sudden seizure. Jonathan heard a strange noise in the bathroom and rushed to check on her.
Jonathan Hill:
I found her slumped over, seizing, convulsing, eyes in the back of her head. I immediately grabbed her and was trying to wake her up, sort of tapping on the face.
V/O:
He sped off to the hospital, and on the way there she came to. At no point at the hospital, or afterwards, could anyone tell them why she had collapsed. It remained a mystery.

Then on social media they saw a post about Jean and Mari’s death, and Vosloo’s suspicions about carbon monoxide poisoning.
Jonathan Hill:
And then we immediately did a search for seizures from carbon monoxide poisoning and everything just made sense and then we realized how close she was from going into a coma.

Taryn Jankes:
I feel incredibly lucky. I didn’t know how close we were to following the same fate. I feel very sorry for the family and those people and ja, I wonder why it wasn’t me. Why did I make it out and they didn’t.
V/O:
Gas geysers in enclosed spaces can be lethal if installed incorrectly.

When gas combusts, it generates heat…but it also produces other gasses like carbon monoxide – a tasteless, colourless, and odourless gas that can overwhelm someone in seconds. It can be deadly in high concentrations.

Monita and Louis Nel discovered this to their horror – also in the shower of the Kliphuis on a weekend getaway in October last year. On the Saturday evening, Monita and Louis went to shower. Monita suddenly felt dizzy.
Monita Nel:
And I can remember I took a towel and I started to dry myself and that was the last thing I can remember.
V/O:
She lost consciousness and collapsed on the floor. When Louis tried to assist her, he also passed out. They were rescued in the nick of time by their son who heard the commotion. Both Louis and Monita recovered, but the incident left the whole family traumatised. They also informed the owner, Gavin Pretorius.
Louis Nel:
Maar ja, ons het dit die Sondag gerapporteer….. die eienaar moet weet daarvan. Dit help nie om stil te bly nie.
V/O:
The Nels also suspected a faulty gas geyser, and contacted Dr Vosloo with their story.
LINK:
There are strict regulations all gas installations must adhere to. The body that oversees the gas industry is the Liquid Petroleum Gas Safety Association of South Africa.
V/O:
Andre Valkenburg speaks on behalf of the Association. The industry is regulated by legislation, and only a certified person may install a gas geyser.
Andre Valkenburg:
It is illegal to do your own gas installation. We find that where incidents have happened and we investigate that specific incident, we find that it was an installation that was done by an unqualified person.
V/O:
All gas appliance installations must carry a Certificate of Compliance, certifying that the installation is safe, and that the correct equipment has been installed.
Andre Valkenburg:
Once you are messing around with the oxygen in a room you are messing around with your life.

Claire:
Can people die?

Andre Valkenburg:
People can die if a heater is installed inside that should not be installed inside.
V/O:
Valkenburg also warns that the public must be careful and ensure adequate ventilation when using any gas appliance, including gas heaters in wintertime.

Confronted with numerous accounts of guests nearly dying in the shower of the Kliphuis, Dr Vosloo commissioned a registered gas practitioner to inspect the gas geyser in the cottage.
LINK:
This is the report by the gas expert. He states that:
• The installation was done by the property owner and not in accordance to the prescribed legal standard
• The gas heater installed inside the bathroom was for outside use only.
• There was no flue pipe to the outside and there was no permanent ventilation in the bathroom
V/O:
We contacted Gavin Pretorius, the owner of the Kliphuis, but he declined to comment, citing the ongoing Police investigation.

It turns out that deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in showers where gas geysers were incorrectly installed, are not so unusual.
LINK:
Over the last few years there were several reports of people dying at holiday resorts because of faulty gas geyser installations.
V/O:
In September 2018, Mark van Rensburg was on a weekend biking trip into Lesotho. At an overnight stop, both Mark’s daughter and his girlfriend Sue Church, were found unconscious in the showers in their respective bungalows. Mark’s daughter was found in time. But Sue was not so lucky. Mark discovered her lifeless body.
Mark van Rensburg:
I ran to her, I picked her up, put her on the bed and I started to give her mouth to mouth. I asked for help. I was giving her mouth to mouth. I knew there was a bigger problem because my daughter had experienced the same thing., but clearly I did not get to her in time. We tried to find out if anybody could do CPR. I am not a professional, but I tried.
V/O:
But it was too late. Sue had died, leaving behind three young children. Mark says there was a gas geyser inside the bathroom where it happened,
there was no flue attached to take exhaust gasses to the outside,
there was no permanent ventilation
and the geyser was denoted for outdoor use only.
He says these pictures of the gas installation were taken the day after Sue’s death.


Since the Lesotho authorities decided not to pursue the case further, Mark asked Dr Reggie Perumal to do a second autopsy – a costly undertaking. Perumal sent blood samples for analysis to a private lab and got the results back within a day.
Dr. Reggie Perumal

Well, her result was over 80% carboxyhaemoglobin. In other words, the carbon monoxide gas bound to the haemoglobin was over 80 %, so it was without doubt the cause of death.
V/O:
Although it could never bring Sue back, uncovering what had caused her death, gave those around her some measure of closure. But Jean and Mari’s families still have no idea when they would be able to get answers from authorities.
LINK:
We contacted the Department of Health in the Eastern Cape and they replied:
V/O:
“The lab results can take many months or sometimes years. But the investigating officer has the authority to pressurise the lab to expedite the process.”

So, for now, all that the grieving families can do, is wait and wonder. Vosloo has vowed that he will not rest until the mystery deaths in the Kliphuis have been solved.
Lawton Vosloo:
I owe it to Jean and Mari to get answers. I owe it to my children to get answers. If we find answers, it will no doubt save other people’s lives.

V/O: Valkenburg also warns that the public must be careful and ensure adequate ventilation when using any gas appliance, including gas heaters in wintertime. Confronted with numerous accounts of guests nearly dying in the shower of the Kliphuis, Dr Vosloo commissioned a registered gas practitioner to inspect the gas geyser in the cottage. LINK: This is the report by the gas expert. He states that: • The installation was done by the property owner and not in accordance to the prescribed legal standard • The gas heater installed inside the bathroom was for outside use only. • There was no flue pipe to the outside and there was no permanent ventilation in the bathroom V/O: We contacted Gavin Pretorius, the owner of the Kliphuis, but he declined to comment, citing the ongoing Police investigation. It turns out that deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in showers where gas geysers were incorrectly installed, are not so unusual. LINK: Over the last few years there were several reports of people dying at holiday resorts because of faulty gas geyser installations. V/O: In September 2018, Mark van Rensburg was on a weekend biking trip into Lesotho. At an overnight stop, both Mark’s daughter and his girlfriend Sue Church, were found unconscious in the showers in their respective bungalows. Mark’s daughter was found in time. But Sue was not so lucky. Mark discovered her lifeless body. Mark van Rensburg: I ran to her, I picked her up, put her on the bed and I started to give her mouth to mouth. I asked for help. I was giving her mouth to mouth. I knew there was a bigger problem because my daughter had experienced the same thing., but clearly I did not get to her in time. We tried to find out if anybody could do CPR. I am not a professional, but I tried. V/O: But it was too late. Sue had died, leaving behind three young children. Mark says there was a gas geyser inside the bathroom where it happened, there was no flue attached to take exhaust gasses to the outside, there was no permanent ventilation and the geyser was denoted for outdoor use only. He says these pictures of the gas installation were taken the day after Sue’s death. Since the Lesotho authorities decided not to pursue the case further, Mark asked Dr Reggie Perumal to do a second autopsy – a costly undertaking. Perumal sent blood samples for analysis to a private lab and got the results back within a day. Dr. Reggie Perumal Well, her result was over 80% carboxyhaemoglobin. In other words, the carbon monoxide gas bound to the haemoglobin was over 80 %, so it was without doubt the cause of death. V/O: Although it could never bring Sue back, uncovering what had caused her death, gave those around her some measure of closure. But Jean and Mari’s families still have no idea when they would be able to get answers from authorities. LINK: We contacted the Department of Health in the Eastern Cape and they replied: V/O: “The lab results can take many months or sometimes years. But the investigating officer has the authority to pressurise the lab to expedite the process.” So, for now, all that the grieving families can do, is wait and wonder. Vosloo has vowed that he will not rest until the mystery deaths in the Kliphuis have been solved. Lawton Vosloo: I owe it to Jean and Mari to get answers. I owe it to my children to get answers. If we find answers, it will no doubt save other people’s lives.

metadata.Further information: FIRST REPORTS The South African Police in Kareedouw have opened an inquest following the death of a couple on a farm in the Kareedouw area. According to police information, the couple and a friend were on the farm Zuuranys, for the weekend. They were staying in a house that is rented out for weekends – a holiday house. It is alleged that the couple went to shower late on Saturday, 25 April 2020 and the friend went to bed. When the friend woke up on Sunday, 26 April 2020, at about 09:00, he noticed that the couple was not in their room. The friend went to the bathroom and discovered that the door was locked from the inside. He kicked in the door and discovered the bodies of the 26-year-old man and his 28-year-old female friend. The police were immediately summoned to the scene and an inquest was opened. No foul play is suspected and the exact cause of death will be determined by the post mortem. ++++++++ The couple who died tragically was Jean Vosloo and Mari Hoon and they were engaged. When the news broke, three more groups of people who stayed over in the Kliphuis and experienced strange effects, in fact they nearly died there. In two instances people lost consciousness in the bathroom while showering and were saved in the nick of time. In another case a man woke up in the night with a massive headache and found his wife unconscious next to him. He was able to revive her once they got outside. The post- mortem yielded no results – the coroner could not find anything. However, blood samples were taken and sent off for analysis. Results are expected in a couple of years. In the meantime, families sit with unanswered questions, and the mystery deaths could be repeated if more people were to stay in that particular holiday house. But with no toxicology reports, the inquest cannot continue and investigations have ground to a halt. Dr Lawton Vosloo, father of Jean, has asked a gas expert to examine the scene, and is disappointed that the coroner would not allow him access to blood samples so it could be tested independently.
